v_hook: Tests sample. Laws prove. And now every proof carries a certificate. Here's what's new in T S laws, version one.
v_mono: Monorepos first. Point T S laws dot json at your packages, and each one keeps its own laws and its own approvers. In VS Code, it follows whichever file you've got open. And running check from the root gives you a result under each project.
v_changed: Add dash dash changed and a branch name, and check only runs the projects your change touches, plus whatever depends on them. Here, core changed, so web and ui come along. Docs doesn't, so it gets skipped.
v_cert: Now, proof certificates. A proved law used to mean you trusted the solver. Now cvc5 writes out its proof in the Alethe format, and a second program, Carcara, checks it. A law only says certified when both agree.
v_cert_real: This is a real run, with cvc5 one point four point two and Carcara. Every proved law comes out certified, the loops included. Under each loop you can read the invariant, and what Eldarica and Golem, two other solvers, made of it.
v_cert_bind: The certificate gets checked again when you accept, and the lock ties it to the exact problem, with hashes of the problem, the proof and the checker. For a loop, the record also holds a hash of its clauses, because the invariant can differ between runs. Set certify to require, and any proved law without a certificate fails the check. Here, every one has one, so the exit status is zero.
v_loops: Loops come next. Z three's Spacer solver finds an invariant using constrained Horn clauses. Then cvc5 proves the clauses with that invariant put in, and Carcara checks the proof, so the invariant itself needs no trust. If you have Eldarica or Golem installed, they cross-check it too. It works on arrays of any length.
v_sec: There are security laws now, and each one carries its C W E number. This function strips one dot dot slash and calls that safe. The law finds an input that gets out of the upload folder, and prints it.
v_deps: T S laws security deps checks the packages your covered code imports against the O S V database. Old lodash and minimist show up with their advisories, and the version that fixes each one. In C I, pass dash dash no cache. The cache is per user, and you want every run to ask again.
v_accept: Accepting a law works two ways. Locally, you run T S laws accept at a terminal and it writes the lock. In GitHub mode, a maintainer can accept on demand from a workflow run. It checks that they have admin or maintain access, and that the branch head hasn't moved since the run. If it has, nothing gets accepted, and it says so.
v_repo: And this repo has it all. It installs cvc5, Carcara, Eldarica and Golem, pinned by checksum, certifies the demo's laws, loops included, checks the invariants with both other solvers, and runs T S laws on its own laws. If a tool's output ever changes, it shows up here first.
v_outro: That's T S laws, one point oh. Install it, write a law, and see what it proves.
